headline: Nikon is re-reviewing a prize-winning microscope video after scientists and online commenters said parts of it looked made up by AI.
score_reason: The row began last week and today's report adds no new finding, only that Nikon is still reviewing.
importance_line: Scientists, contest judges and anyone who trusts published science images are affected, because the case shows AI-processed pictures can pass as real data, but it is still unclear whether the contest's rule against generative AI was broken since the entrant says AI was used only in post-processing.
summary: Gizmodo reports that Nikon, which sponsors a microscope video contest, says it is “carefully re-reviewing” the winning entry after commenters, including a university bioengineer, questioned the red, blue and purple shapes shown under the moving cells, and one pointed out, according to CNN, that the video carries Google's SynthID AI watermark. The entrant, Ning Xu of the National University of Singapore, says the footage of the cells is real and AI was only used to separate and color structures in processed data, and the contest's organizers had no update.
